description: MVP Phase - GitHub-integrated collaborative markdown editor with real-time editing, repository selection, folder navigation, and commenting system

introduction.overview: A real-time collaborative markdown editor that allows multiple users to edit documents simultaneously with seamless synchronization, similar to Google Docs or Microsoft Teams documents. The system is backed by GitHub for version control and storage, with automatic commits that are transparent to users. Users can also add review comments in sidebar threads to facilitate collaboration and feedback.

phases.PoC: Prove that real-time collaborative editing works with minimal features
phases.MVP: Production-ready version with authentication, GitHub integration, and comments

goals: Enable real-time collaborative editing of markdown documents with multiple concurrent users
Provide seamless GitHub integration with automatic background commits (no manual Git operations)
Implement sidebar comment threads for document reviews and discussions
Support basic markdown formatting (headings, bold, italic, lists, links)
Authenticate users securely via GitHub OAuth
Ensure conflict-free editing experience through Yjs CRDT real-time sync technology
nonGoals: Mobile native apps: Web-based only (responsive design acceptable)
Rich text (WYSIWYG) editor mode: Markdown source editing only
Real-time voice/video chat: Communication through comments only
Integrations with tools other than GitHub: No Notion, Confluence, or other platform syncs
AI-powered features: No auto-completion, grammar checking, or content generation
Spreadsheet/table editor: Tables rendered as markdown only, no Excel-like editing
Presentation mode: Focus on document editing, not slideshow creation

uiux: Clean, minimal interface: Focus on content, reduce UI clutter
Responsive design: Should work on desktop and tablet (mobile is non-goal but should degrade gracefully)
Split-pane editor: Markdown source on left, preview on right (or toggle view)
Sidebar for comments: Slides in from right, doesn't obstruct main editor
User avatars: Use GitHub profile pictures for authenticated users
Color coding: Each collaborator gets a distinct color for cursor and highlights
accessibility: Keyboard shortcuts for common formatting actions
Proper ARIA labels for screen readers

architecture.database: PostgreSQL for users, comments, and metadata (documents stored in GitHub)

githubIntegration.repositoryStructure: Users can select any GitHub repository they have write access to
githubIntegration.commentStorage: Store comments in PostgreSQL database for faster queries
githubIntegration.commitStrategy: Batch changes from multiple users into single commits every 30-60 seconds to avoid excessive commit history
githubIntegration.authentication: GitHub OAuth with encrypted token storage

realTimeSync.conflictResolution: Yjs CRDT ensures character-level merging without conflicts
realTimeSync.networkResilience: Handle reconnection gracefully with exponential backoff, queue changes during disconnection

performance.documentSizeLimit: Start with reasonable limits (e.g., 1MB per document) to ensure real-time sync performance
performance.concurrentUsers: Support at least 10 concurrent users per document without degradation
performance.websocketPooling: Optimize server resources for many simultaneous documents
performance.caching: 5-minute TTL for repository lists and file trees

security.oauth: Validate OAuth tokens, use HTTPS only
security.tokenEncryption: AES-256-GCM encryption for stored GitHub tokens
security.rateLimiting: Prevent abuse of GitHub API and WebSocket connections
security.inputSanitization: Prevent XSS in markdown preview and comments

PoC.realTimeSync: Multiple users can edit simultaneously without merge conflicts
PoC.latency: Changes propagate to all users within 1 second
PoC.concurrentUsers: At least 3-5 users can edit the same document simultaneously
PoC.stability: PoC runs for 30+ minutes without crashes or data corruption

MVP.collaborationEffectiveness: Users can edit documents concurrently without experiencing merge conflicts or data loss
MVP.syncLatency: Changes propagate to all users within 1 second under normal network conditions
MVP.autoSaveReliability: 99.9% of edits successfully committed to GitHub without user intervention
MVP.userAdoption: Users prefer this tool over manual Git workflows for collaborative markdown editing
MVP.commentEngagement: At least 30% of documents have at least one comment thread (indicating review/collaboration usage)
MVP.documentAccessibility: Users can access any document from the GitHub repo within 2 seconds

successMetrics.Horizon1: To be defined based on feature set implemented

MVP.question: How do comments remain anchored when the document text changes around them?
MVP.recommendation: Use character offsets with Yjs position tracking for automatic updates

MVP.question: What's the upper limit of simultaneous editors per document?
MVP.recommendation: Start with 10-20 user limit for MVP, test and optimize in Horizon 1

openQuestions.Horizon1: To be defined when Horizon 1 planning begins

approach: Start with basic WebSocket server and simple name-based authentication
Integrate Yjs for CRDT (y-websocket for WebSocket provider, store document in memory with Y.Doc)
Add basic markdown preview (react-markdown, split-pane layout)
Implement cursor sharing (Yjs awareness API, assign random colors)
Test with multiple browser windows locally (3-5 tabs to simulate multi-user editing)
PoC.status: Completed - All PoC user stories implemented and passing

Implement GitHub OAuth and session management with encrypted token storage

Create repository selector and folder navigation UI
Implement automatic GitHub commits with conflict resolution
Build commenting system (database schema, sidebar UI, anchoring logic)
Add GitHub avatars to user presence indicators
MVP.status: In Progress - US-MVP-008 through US-MVP-007 defined and ready for implementation

Horizon1.approach: To be defined when Horizon 1 planning begins

userStories.title: Set up PostgreSQL and Redis with Docker Compose
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a database and session store to support user authentication, encrypted tokens, and comments.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml created in root directory
PostgreSQL service configured (port 5432, volume for data persistence)
Redis service configured (port 6379) for session store
Adminer service configured (port 8080) for database GUI
Environment variables in .env: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL
Database migrations directory created: db/migrations/
Migration 001: Create users table (id, github_id, username, email, avatar_url, created_at, updated_at)
Migration 002: Create user_tokens table (id, user_id, provider, access_token_encrypted, access_token_iv, access_token_auth_tag, token_type, scope, expires_at, created_at, updated_at)
Migration 003: Create comments table (id, user_id, document_path, repo_owner, repo_name, char_start, char_end, text, resolved, created_at, updated_at)
Migration 004: Create comment_replies table (id, comment_id, user_id, text, created_at, updated_at)
Migration runner implemented in apps/api/src/db/migrate.ts
Database connection pool configured in apps/api/src/db/connection.ts
Environment variables: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (32-byte hex)
README.md updated with Docker Compose instructions
Typecheck passes
Verify: docker-compose up starts all services successfully
userStories.notes: Completed: All database infrastructure set up successfully. Docker Compose running PostgreSQL, Redis, and Adminer. All migrations applied successfully. Typecheck passes.

userStories.title: Implement GitHub service layer with Octokit
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a service layer to interact with GitHub API for repository and file operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Install octokit package: npm install octokit
GitHubService class created in apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts
Method: listUserRepositories(token) - GET /user/repos with affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member, filter by push permission
Method: getRepositoryTree(owner, repo, token) - GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1
Method: getFileContent(owner, repo, path, token) - GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}, decode Base64
Method: updateFile(owner, repo, path, content, sha, message, token) - PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}
Method: createFile(owner, repo, path, content, message, token) - PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}
Uses authenticated Octokit instances per user token
Implements retry logic with exponential backoff for rate limit errors (403)
Error handling for 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 403 (rate limit/permission)
Structured logging for all GitHub API calls with req.logger
Caches repository lists in-memory with 5-minute TTL using Map
Typecheck passes
Unit tests for each method with mocked Octokit responses
userStories.notes: Completed: GitHubService fully implemented with all methods (listUserRepositories, getRepositoryTree, getFileContent, updateFile, createFile). Retry logic with exponential backoff for 403 rate limit errors. Structured logging integrated. In-memory caching with 5-minute TTL. Dependency injection pattern added for testability. Comprehensive unit tests (17 tests) with 100% coverage. All tests passing, typecheck passes.

acceptanceCriteria: Install dependencies: passport, passport-github2, express-session, connect-redis

Environment variables: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, SESSION_SECRET
Passport.js configured with GitHubStrategy in apps/api/src/config/passport.ts
OAuth scopes requested: 'repo user:email'
User profile (github_id, username, email, avatar_url) stored in PostgreSQL users table
GitHub access token encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored in user_tokens table
Token encryption service created in apps/api/src/services/token.service.ts
express-session configured with Redis store (connect-redis)
Auth routes created: GET /auth/github (initiate OAuth), GET /auth/github/callback (handle callback), GET /auth/logout, GET /auth/user (current user info)
Authentication middleware created: apps/api/src/middleware/authenticate.ts - checks session
Token validation middleware created: apps/api/src/middleware/validateGitHubToken.ts - verifies token with GitHub API
Frontend login page with 'Sign in with GitHub' button redirects to /auth/github
After successful auth, redirect to repository selection page
Unauthenticated users redirected to login page for protected routes
Replaces PoC name-based authentication (remove NamePrompt component)
Typecheck passes
Test OAuth flow in browser
userStories.notes: Completed: GitHub OAuth authentication fully implemented. All backend services (token encryption, passport config, auth routes, middleware) created and tested. Frontend login and repository selector pages implemented. All acceptance criteria met. Typecheck passes. 32 tests passing (17 tests for token service, 15 for existing GitHub service).

userStories.notes: Completed: Full document browser implementation with folder navigation. Backend route GET /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/tree with tree filtering for .md files. GitHubService.filterMarkdownTree() filters tree to only show markdown files and folders containing them. In-memory cache with 5-minute TTL implemented. Frontend DocumentBrowser component with collapsible tree view, breadcrumb navigation (repository path), file size display. Empty, loading, and error states with retry button. Click file to navigate to editor route. 51 tests passing (34 new tests for tree functionality). Typecheck passes. Note: Last commit date/author metadata deferred as it requires additional GitHub API calls and is not critical for MVP - files show size metadata instead.

userStories.notes: Completed: Full document creation functionality implemented. Backend POST /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/files route with validation, error handling, and cache invalidation. userStories.title: Automatic GitHub commits with conflict handling
userStories.description: As a user, I want my changes automatically saved to GitHub without manual commits, with proper handling of concurrent edits.
acceptanceCriteria: Editor route: /repositories/:owner/:repo/edit/:path loads document content
Backend route: GET /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/files/:path fetches file content and SHA
Backend uses GitHubService.getFileContent() to fetch file from GitHub
File content loaded into Yjs Y.Doc and synced to all connected users
Yjs maintains real-time collaboration as in PoC (no changes to Yjs behavior)
Background job created: apps/api/src/jobs/githubSync.job.ts runs every 30-60 seconds
Background job checks for modified Yjs documents (Y.Doc with changes since last commit)
On save, batch commits from multiple concurrent editors into single commit
Commit message format: 'Update {filename} - {timestamp} - Editors: {user1, user2, user3}'
Uses GitHubService.updateFile(owner, repo, path, content, currentSHA, message, token)
Automatic conflict resolution on 409 response: Fetch latest SHA, merge Yjs state with latest content, retry commit with new SHA
Visual save status indicator in editor header: 'Saving...', 'All changes saved', 'Conflict resolved', 'Error saving'
Rate limit monitoring: Log warning if approaching 4500/5000 requests per hour
Document state preserved in Yjs during conflict resolution (no data loss)
Yjs queues changes if user closes browser before save completes
Error notifications for save failures with retry button
Typecheck passes
Test with two users editing same file simultaneously, trigger conflict
